verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents a public Realtime SFU API over standard HTTPS. Clients use it to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video and data, and the docs cite concrete endpoints such as `PUT .../datachannels/update`. A probe also found a machine-readable OpenAPI spec on the developer docs site, which suits agent-driven use. Missing for 10: evidence that the OpenAPI spec specifically covers the Realtime/RealtimeKit endpoints, detailed API reference content for RealtimeKit server-side control, and independent hands-on corroboration of driving the product through the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Use standard HTTPS APIs and WebRTC from browsers, embedded firmware, native applications, and servers.
Grant or revoke without re-pulling via `PUT .../datachannels/update`.
PROBE openapi: HTTP 200 at https://developers.cloudflare.com/openapi.json — contains "openapi" key
